title: Rework autoscaler capacity queue and node lifecycle to reduce spurious evictions
creator: Hannah Li
description:
Problem: The current GPU autoscaler and capacity planner reconciler produce transient over-evictions and noisy node teardown activity during bursty scheduling. Root causes we identified: (1) a non-idempotent node lifecycle code path that double-counts capacity race conditions during rapid add/remove, (2) a synchronous reconciler that processes high event burst on the main loop leading to tail latency spikes, and (3) outdated Kubernetes client (client-go) behavior around watch reconnects that exacerbates duplicate events. These issues lead to spurious preemptive node drains, increased pod scheduling latency, and oscillation in pool sizes under synthetic and production bursts.

Goal: Refactor the autoscaler reconciliation and node lifecycle to be deterministic, idempotent, and asynchronous; reduce spurious evictions by >50% in synthetic burst tests and reduce per-request 95th latency for allocation paths by 25%. Deliver a safe migration that can be canaried on a small Dedicated pool and rolled out with automatic rollback on regressions.

Proposed changes:
- Replace the current monolithic reconciler with a rate-limited capacity workqueue (sharded by pool id) to smooth bursts and deduplicate events.
- Convert node lifecycle handling to an explicit state machine (PendingAllocation -> Occupied -> Draining -> Terminated) with idempotent transitions and persisted last-applied intent in the pool metadata.
- Centralize capacity accounting into a single CP consistent writer using optimistic concurrency (compare-and-swap) to avoid double-free/over-commit races.
- Upgrade client-go from 1.25.x to 1.29.x to pick up improved informer reconnect semantics and watch dedup optimizations. Documented compatibility concerns and test matrix included below.
- Add end-to-end synthetic workload tests and microbenchmarks for the reconciler under bursty create/delete patterns; add Prometheus metrics for workqueue depth and average processing time.

Acceptance criteria:
- Integration tests pass in CI (kube v1.26 and v1.29 matrix). Unit tests for state machine cover all transitions and error handling.
- Synthetic load test demonstrates >=50% fewer evictions compared to baseline (run script workload/eviction-burst.sh with seed X).
- 95th percentile allocation latency reduced by >=25% in the canary pool.
- No data plane customer workloads experience increased error rates during a staged rollout.
- Migration plan exercised once on a non-production Dedicated pool and sign-off from infra and SRE.

Migration and rollout plan:
1) Merge feature branch behind a runtime flag (autoscaler.v2.enabled=false by default).
2) Run canary on pool-id:dedicated-canary-3 with flag set to true for 48h; monitor the metrics below.
3) If canary is healthy, incrementally enable on 10% of pools for 24h, then 50% for 24h, then 100%.
4) Automated rollback if eviction.rate > baseline*0.9 or allocation.errors > baseline + 1.5x stdev.

Key metrics to monitor:
- autoscaler.evictions.total
- autoscaler.evictions.by_pool
- capacity.planner.alloc.latency_ms.{p50,p95,p99}
- autoscaler.workqueue.depth
- node.lifecycle.transition_errors
- gpu.pool.available_nodes

Testing and benchmarks:
- Local microbenchmark harness: tools/autoscaler/bench.sh. Baseline run: avg CPU 120m/core, p95 latency 180ms. After refactor (branch ENG-30977-refactor) local benchmark: avg CPU 95m/core (-21%), p95 latency 135ms (-25%), simulated eviction reduction 58%.
- CI e2e job: e2e/autoscaler-burst (kube v1.26, v1.29) added; must be green before merging.

Risks and trade-offs:
- Upgrading client-go carries risk of subtle incompatibilities with some on-prem Kubernetes versions; mitigated by test matrix and opt-in flag.
- Moving to optimistic concurrency increases transient CAS failures which must be properly retried; added exponential backoff and instrumentation.
- Introducing persisted intent adds schema migration for pool metadata; plan includes a no-op backward-compatible format for rollbacks.

Implementation notes and links:
- Design doc: https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/FLEET/Autoscaler+Workqueue+and+Node+State+Machine
- Draft PR with implementation and bench harness: https://github.com/redwood-inference/redwood/pull/4672
- Synthetic workload script: https://github.com/redwood-inference/test-harness/blob/main/workloads/eviction_burst.sh
- Observability dashboard: https://grafana.redwood.ai/d/abc123/autoscaler-health

Next steps:
- Finish state machine implementation and add persistence layer (ETA 2 days).
- Add e2e CI job and run baseline vs branch comparison (ETA 3 days).
- Coordinate client-go upgrade with platform-infra and support (ETA 1 week for approvals).
